items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Topics 9:1
items.html: The Parsa is the discernment of the end of half of the upper Partzuf, which is the discernment of the name MB, as above in answer 95. However, since there are two points of ending — from the side of the middle line it is at the chest, and from the side of the extremities it is at the Tabur, as above — the Parsa too stands there diagonally: it begins at the chest, below the middle line, and ends at the Tabur, below the extremities, as above. And when you measure the place relative to AVI Ila’in in their Gadlut, which are the discernment of AB, whose legs end at the Tabur, as is known, you will find that the Parsa begins at the end of the belly of AVI, where the Yesod of Ima is, and from there descends and extends down to the Tabur of AA — that is, to the end of the legs of AVI, as explained in the words of the ARI (Etz Chaim, Gate 14, Chapter 3).
